\"The Windows desktop\", or \"Switch bac: "The Windows desktop", or "Switch back to the Windows desktop" on the desktop's settings button, brings Explorer back at once. If the desktop ever does not respond: Ctrl+Shift+Esc, "Run new task", UltraDesktop --restore-desktop.
A program that starts with the desktop o: A program that starts with the desktop opens minimized a few seconds after it - unless it is running already - and keeps working in the background: ChatCube receives messages, UltraMail fetches mail and shows the unread count on the desktop's mail icon. The desktop's settings button offers the same choice on its right-click menu.
An application registers again the next: An application registers again the next time it starts or shows a notification, so removing does no harm to one you keep.
An application uses a change the next ti: An application uses a change the next time it starts. The command line (--lang) and the ULTRACANVAS_LANG variable override this setting for one start.
At sign-in, for this account: beside Exp: At sign-in, for this account: beside Explorer, UltraDesktop starts with the session and Explorer's taskbar hides itself, while Explorer's tray, notifications and Start menu keep working - from now on. Instead of Explorer, UltraDesktop is the whole desktop from the next sign-in: it shows the programs' tray icons and offers sign out, restart and shut down; Explorer does not start, and with it go the parts of Windows it hosts (the Start menu, the quick settings, the notification centre). Should UltraDesktop fail, Explorer starts in its place for that session.
